chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abdul Hamid ibn Sa'd, said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who sold goods on credit for three years from a wealthy man, whose right and wealth are trusted. Would he purify that wealth every year that passes by, or would he purify it when he takes it? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, but he purifies it when he takes it.' I said to him: 'For how long does he purify it?' He said: 'For three years.'

key_terms.بَيْعاً إِلَى ثَلَاثِ سِنِينَ: Sale on credit for three years

ai.seo_question: When is Zakat due on a debt received after a delay?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the timing of Zakat liability on deferred payments (dayn), establishing that the obligation arises only upon actual receipt rather than annually during the waiting period. The Imam specifies a three-year holding period (hawl) for calculating the due amount, reflecting the Shia scholarly view on the assessment of debts from solvent debtors. This ruling provides practical guidance for financial planning, ensuring Zakat is not prematurely levied on uncollected wealth.
